P171.s0.text: **Diagnosis.** The new species is similar to T. baishanzuensis sp. nov., but it can be easily recognized from latter by the bicolored femora.

P171.s1.text: From other species of east and southeast China, it can be easily recognized by the bicolored abdomen.

P175.s0.text: **Description.** The new species is similar to T. baishanzuensis sp. nov. in most aspects except for the following characters: abdominal tergites III–VII each with a longer and more distinct triangular, mediobasal, golden tomentose patch; femora each with median dark mark and apical dark mark, although the apical dark markings of the forelegs are less distinct.

P176.s1.text: Aedeagus (Figs 88–95) slender, median lobe gradually narrowed apicad with round apex in ventral view, apex of median lobe expanded dorsad in lateral view; paramere relatively long, apex wide and round with approximately 11 setae around the apical margin.

P185.s0.text: **Diagnosis.** The new species is the only brachypterous species of the genus so far that is known from mainland China, except for a potential record of a brachypterous T. malaisei, from which it can be separated as indicated above.

P185.s1.text: The T. malaisei specimens from the type locality have rather short elytra and developed hindwings, which may be functional or not since the palisade fringe on tergite VII is very narrow.

P185.s2.text: Thoracostrongylus miyakei from Taiwan also has weakly developed, non-functional hind wings and no palisade fringe on tergite VII, which differs from the new species by pronotum without impunctate midline.

P187.s0.text: **Description.** The new species is almost identical to T. malaisei, from which it differs, in addition to the different aedeagus, by the differently colored labrum, which is reddish with each lobe with a large, dark brown, central spot (in T. malaisei with a black medial margin along medial excision).

P187.s1.text: Most specimens of T. malaisei have at least a very narrow palisade fringe on tergite VII, which is lacking only in the single specimen from Yunnan.

P188.s1.text: Aedeagus (Figs 98–101) slender and long, median lobe swollen in middle third and then narrowed apicad in ventral view; in lateral view, median lobe with subapical tooth on dorsal side in apical sixth; paramere rather wide, subparallel-sided, apical margin with slight medial notch, with approximately seven setae.
